claims.claim: The city’s case also points to the broader market impact: Wall Street firms reportedly pay up to $100,000 a month for the service, and the company’s stock has fallen below $10 after briefly trading near $62 when it went public two years ago.
claims.bestSource: Lawsuit seeks to ban Trump Media from charging for early access to president’s posts on US policy - Sun Sentinel
claims.evidence: The early access service comes as the publicly traded Trump Media loses hundreds of millions of dollars each quarter and its stock has dropped below $10 from $62 shortly after going public two years ago. NEW YORK (AP) — President Donald Trump was sued in federal court Wednesday to stop him from making money off a new, paid service at his Truth Social company offering early, exclusive access to his posts on U.S. policy. Trump is the largest shareholder of Trump Media, owning more than 40% of its shares through a trust. The new subscription service rolled out earlier this month is charging Wall Street firms as much as $100,000 a month to trade off the market-moving posts before others. “Information from President Trump is disseminated by countless platforms and news outlets, many of which offer subscription APIs,” it said in a statement, using the acronym for the fast access service. “Now, left wing activists are trying to wrongfully weaponize the courts to censor him again and harm our shareholders.” “A president selling priority access to news he himself generates for the benefit of a private company he controls is so blatantly corrupt and unconstitutional that it would have been hard to even fathom just a few years ago,” said Seth Stern, chief of advocacy at the Freedom of the Press Foundation, a plaintiff in the case along with news outlet The Intercept.
